extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the kinds of publications NIRI produces and the purposes/qualities those publications are intended to serve for investor relations professionals. Useful for understanding what content formats and standards NIRI emphasizes for IR communications and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep practitioners on the forefront
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything NIRI publishes is designed to keep you on the forefront of the latest news, approaches and ideas in investor relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications should present up-to-date news, emerging approaches, and fresh ideas so readers remain current in IR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include relevant research findings
rubrics_metrics.description: From the most relevant research findings to proven best practices, NIRI’s publications will keep you in the know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should incorporate current, relevant research and data-driven findings that inform IR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey proven best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: From the most relevant research findings to proven best practices, NIRI’s publications will keep you in the know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable, proven practices that IR professionals can apply; emphasize practical applicability and tested approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive domain definition (IR Competency Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: This comprehensive guide defines the major domains of IR practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources intended to be comprehensive should map the full set of IR competencies and clearly define major domains and areas of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable planning and response to change (Think Tank Reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: These reports enable NIRI, IR practitioners and IR stakeholders to plan for and respond to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical reports should identify trends, scenarios, and recommendations that help stakeholders anticipate and react to industry or regulatory shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential reference materials (Books)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that investor relations professionals should not be without.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-form works should serve as go-to references: comprehensive, authoritative, and enduringly useful for IR professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide relevant data and vital information (Research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant data and information on issues vital to the practice of Investor Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research outputs must focus on issues that are critical to IR, supplying reliable data, analysis, and clear implications for practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative expert insights (IR Update Magazine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover valuable insights and information from the leading experts of the field with NIRI’s award-winning magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magazine content should feature contributions from recognized experts, offering insight, interpretation, and practical guidance; credibility (e.g., awards) is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely regulatory and compliance alerts (Executive Alerts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking information on regulatory and compliance issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alerts must be fast, concise, and focused on regulatory/compliance developments that materially affect IR; timeliness and clarity are paramount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current member sentiment / rapid-survey results (Pulse Polls)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulse polls should report recent, topical survey results that capture member views and trends; emphasize recency and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular communications cadence (IR Update Weekly)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsletters should be periodic (weekly), summarizing current items of interest for IR professionals in a concise, consumable format.
